dashboard.groups_empty: Groups let you train on a subset — one side of the family, a project team, or exactly the people you keep mixing up.
dashboard.lede_bad: Something in the storage layer is not healthy — the details below say which part. This page is deliberately blunt because a half-working database is worse than a stopped one.
dashboard.lede_ok: Storage, schema and write access all check out. The cabinet holds the people and their photos; the trainer that drills them arrives in M2.
dashboard.m1_body: People, photos, groups and search, plus the login gate that makes this safe to put behind the house reverse proxy. Photos are downscaled on import and their metadata is dropped before they touch the database.

stats.bars_label: Answers per day over the last {days} days, peaking at {peak}
stats.calibration_based: Based on {n} {answer} where you said how sure you were.
stats.calibration_empty: You have not told Kith how sure you were yet. The answer screen offers two small faces once you have answered — "not sure" and "sure" — and this panel fills in. The part worth having is the mistakes you were certain about.
stats.calibration_negative_post: accurate when you feel sure — the mistakes worth reading twice.
stats.calibration_neutral: Your certainty barely tracks your accuracy: worth knowing before you trust a hunch.
stats.calibration_positive: Feeling certain is worth about {points} points of accuracy to you — which is a healthy gap, not a flattering one.
stats.confusion_explainer: These are the mistakes worth drilling: you know both faces, which is exactly why they collide.
stats.data_explainer_post: the export. Take a copy before a restore, and every so often for no better reason than that it takes one click.
stats.data_explainer_pre: Everything Kith knows — every person, every photo, every review — lives in a single SQLite file, which is why the backup
stats.difficulty_explainer: Scheduler difficulty, 1 to 10, over cards you have actually answered. A cabinet piling up on the right means a lot of faces that need a lot of reminding.
stats.empty_hint: Add a person with a photo and this page starts counting.
stats.heading: Progress
stats.known_explainer: A face counts as known once you could name it after a month away — currently {rate} % of the cabinet. {n} {card} in all, {suspended} suspended.
stats.no_confusion: Nothing has been swapped yet, or nothing has been answered.
stats.no_groups: No groups yet — a group is the quickest way to say "the people from work".
stats.replace_error.confirm: Nothing was replaced: the word REPLACE was not typed.
stats.replace_error.corrupt: Nothing was replaced: that database failed its integrity check.
stats.replace_error.huge: Nothing was replaced: that file is larger than 1 GB.
stats.replace_error.nofile: Nothing was replaced: no file arrived.
stats.replace_error.notsqlite: Nothing was replaced: that file is not a SQLite database.
stats.replace_error.tables: Nothing was replaced: that database is missing Kith tables.
stats.replace_error.version: Nothing was replaced: that database was written by a different Kith schema.
stats.replaced_post: , so this is undoable by hand if it was the wrong file.
stats.replaced_pre: The database it replaced was kept beside it as
stats.restore_explainer: This replaces everything currently in the cabinet, and only a file that is a readable Kith database on this schema will be accepted. Whatever it replaces is snapshotted first.
stats.retention_line: {answered} answers over {active_days} {day}, {correct} of them right — {rate} %. That is a floor rather than a flattering number: every hard day is in it.
stats.storage_line: {total} MB in one SQLite file — {photos} {photo} taking {size} MB ({each} KB each, downscaled to fit). Nothing else on this machine, and nothing anywhere else: the backup is that one file.

train.empty: Nothing to train on yet — the cabinet is empty.
train.force: Practise anyway — ignore what's due and go over these faces again.
train.force_note: Nothing is ever lost by it; the schedule just gets an extra look.
train.heading: Train
train.hint_after: and a settled one climbs one rung at a time, so ticking both multiple choice and free recall lets a face move up as it settles. Free recall is the hard one; multiple choice needs enough faces in the cabinet to make the options real; the confusion drill is only offered for a pair you have actually mixed up. New faces are always shown to you once before they are tested — that part is not optional.
train.hint_before: Tick what you are willing to be asked — nothing outside this list is ever asked of you. Of the modes you tick, a shaky face is asked the
train.missing_body: That session does not exist — it may have been from a database you have since replaced.
train.no_modes_backwards: reverse and listening come online for faces you have already met once - tick multiple choice alongside them for a first run, or practise anyway
train.no_modes_needs_people: the enabled modes need more people than the cabinet has
train.no_modes_nothing_to_ask: the modes you ticked have nothing to ask here - the confusion drill needs a mix-up you have actually made
train.no_people: nobody to train on with that filter
train.nothing_due: nothing is due and no new faces were asked for - tick 'practise anyway' and start again to go over these faces regardless
